free_tier.stated: EUR 4.90/month: 1 Ryzen core (shared), 6,144 MB RAM, 50 GB NVMe, 51,200 GB/month bandwidth, 0.98 Gbps port, IPv4 and IPv6, Paris France. A second EUR 4.90 card offers 2 Epyc cores, 8,192 MB RAM and 80 GB NVMe in Frankfurt, and a EUR 6.60 card offers 160 GB NVMe. The vendor's own cloud-server page states the Ryzen VPS range as 1 to 8 cores, 6 to 48 GB RAM, 50 to 400 GB NVMe, 50 TB of traffic included a month, and that prices there are exclusive of VAT.

egress.terms: 50 TB a month included and up to 300 TB extra, per the vendor range table (free_allowance is in GB a month); the price of the extra traffic is not stated on the page read

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: the cloud-server page is a configurator (CPU, location, then slider ranges); VNC console, ISO mount and up/down grades through the client area are documented; no published API was found on the pages read
chaining: 50 TB a month stated plainly on the vendor's own page for EUR 4.90 exclusive of VAT, with 6 GB of RAM, puts it just behind LowHosting's 51,200 GB claim in allowance and far ahead of the 5 TB at Luxvps and the 1 TB at LeapSwitch

limits.value: 50 TB (51,200 GB) a month included, with up to 300 TB of extra traffic sold; the vendor states prices exclusive of VAT, so the payable figure is above EUR 4.90 wherever VAT applies. The 50 GB NVMe is the limit for anything cached locally, and extra HDD is EUR 2 per TB

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the tracker's profile text describes the operator as owning its hardware in ISO/IEC 27001 colocation, which is the tracker's claim and was not checked

evidence.proved: Layer7 card, with the euro sign written EUR for ASCII: the price line prints 4.90 with the euro sign and '/ month'; the rest quotes verbatim as '1 Ryzen Cores (shared)', '6,144 MB RAM', '50 GB NVMe', '51,200 GB/month bandwidth', '0.98 Gbps port speed', 'IPv4 + IPv6', 'Paris France'. All 12 cards on the page carry an order link

range table quoted for the AMD Ryzen 9950X3D line: 'VPS | 1 - 8 | 6 - 48 GB | 50 GB - 400 GB | up to 3 disks 0 - 5 TB each | 50 TB incl. + up to 300 TB extra', with 'Prices here are exclusive VAT' and 'up to 3x additional HDD disks at 2,- EUR per TB'; location Frankfurt/Main and Paris
standard features quoted: 'KVM hardwarevirtualized, CPU pass-through', '1x IPv4 incl. rDNS', '1x IPv6 incl. rDNS', 'Remote Console (VNC)', 'individual ISO mount', 'up to 2500 Mbit/s Connectivity'

notes: The configurator rendered ranges rather than per-plan prices, so the EUR 4.90 figure is the tracker's and the confidence is reported; the vendor page does confirm the included traffic, the VAT exclusion and the HDD add-on price, which is why those three are recorded from it. The tracker's '0.98 Gbps' looks like its rounding of a 1 Gbps port; the vendor states connectivity up to 2.5 Gbit/s. Would settle: the per-plan price grid behind the configurator, and whether the EUR 2 per TB HDD survives at order time for a 20 TiB configuration.
